abstract: The binding of a panel of lectins to histological sections of seminomas was studied. The findings were correlated with different clinical parameters. Concanavalin A and wheat germ agglutinin stained all seminomas whereas horse gram (DBA) and peanut agglutinin did not stain the tumor cells. A varying staining pattern was found with lectins from castor bean (RCA I), soy bean (SBA) and gorse (UEA I) indicating a heterogeneity of the tumor cell population. In the seminomas that were derived from undescended testis there were more cases that showed positive staining with soy bean agglutinin, which shows that the intra-abdominal location of the seminoma might cause changes in the cellular metabolism resulting in glycoconjugates different from those in descended tumors. No correlation was found between the lectin staining and the prognosis, stage or metastasis of the tumor.
abstract_ja: セミノーマの組織切片に対する一連のレクチンの結合を検討し、その所見を各種臨床パラメータと相関させた。コンカナバリンAとWGAはすべてのセミノーマを染色したが、DBAとPNAは腫瘍細胞を染色しなかった。RCA I、SBA、UEA Iでは染色パターンが多様で、腫瘍細胞集団の不均一性が示された。停留精巣由来のセミノーマでは、SBA陽性例が多く、腹腔内という位置が細胞代謝を変化させ、下降精巣の腫瘍とは異なる糖鎖を生じさせる可能性が示唆された。レクチン染色と予後、病期、転移との間に相関は認められなかった。
